clue.text: Check a lighter for big game

parts.note: to check something is to test it
a match is something you light a fire with, a lighter

explanation.surface: Someone asks a friend for a light before going out to hunt big game.
explanation.walkthrough: A TEST MATCH is an international cricket match lasting several days, the biggest fixture in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket international between national sides is the most important kind of fixture, hence a big game.

clue.text: Sit up, taking in the church taxes

indicators.note: taking in means the reversed letters swallow the next word inside them
in a down clue, up means the word Sit is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to sit up straight is being lectured about money owed to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit up' reads as an order to sit straight, but in a down clue 'up' turns the word over, and 'taking in' wraps the result around the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the tenth parts of produce paid each year to support the parish clergy.

clue.text: A companion in the ring improves one's chances of winning the fight

definitions.text: A companion in the ring improves one's chances of winning the fight

parts.words: A companion in the ring improves one's chances of winning the fight
parts.note: a boxer trains with someone who practises bouts with them, and that practice helps them win the real contest

explanation.surface: A boxer's helper in the ring makes victory more likely.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a second or a cornerman helping during the fight, but the help comes in training beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's training opponent spars with them in practice bouts to prepare for a real contest.

clue.text: Fish, whipped cream, and Elk

indicators.note: cream is whipped into a new shape, so these letters are beaten into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd menu: fish, whipped cream and elk meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped' looks like part of the menu, but it is the anagram signal for CREAM + ELK.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an oily sea species with striped blue-green skin, often eaten smoked.

clue.text: Throw money about? It's a chancy business

definitions.meaning: to flip a coin into the air, read literally as throwing cash
an even-odds matter that could go either way

explanation.surface: Spending money freely is a risky way to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw money about' usually means spend wildly; here it means flipping a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip has even odds, so any uncertain outcome is likened to one.

clue.text: Site of Normandy landings that proved bad for the English army

definitions.text: Site of Normandy landings that proved bad for the English army

parts.words: Site of Normandy landings that proved bad for the English army
parts.note: Normandy landings brings D-Day of 1944 to mind, but the landing meant here is the Norman invasion of 1066, which defeated King Harold's English army

explanation.surface: A place where an invasion from Normandy went badly for the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Normandy landings' points to 1944, but the clue means William the Conqueror's arrival in 1066 and the battle near the Sussex coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1066 battle in which William of Normandy defeated King Harold is named after this Sussex town.

clue.text: To encourage an appreciative audience, will give it!

definitions.meaning: to urge someone on or lift their spirits

definitions.text: an appreciative audience, will give it!
definitions.meaning: a pleased crowd shouts out its approval

explanation.surface: To spur on a delighted audience, give them something to shout about.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten or urge on is one sense; the other is a shout of approval from a crowd.

clue.text: TV dancer, gone out to get music centre

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A television dancer, having left, goes off to a concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone out' reads as one phrase, but 'gone' is part of the anagram and only 'out' signals it. COVENT GARDEN is home to London's Royal Opera House.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Royal Opera House stands in this district, making it a centre of opera and ballet.

clue.text: Contest at which we run till we drop

definitions.text: Contest at which we run till we drop

parts.words: Contest at which we run till we drop
parts.note: run till we drop sounds like exhaustion, but runners carry an item on a utensil and lose when it falls

explanation.surface: An endurance race where competitors keep going until they collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till we drop' means until exhausted; here it is the egg that drops off the spoon. This is a school sports-day race.
explanation.definitionFit: In this school sports-day race each runner balances an egg on a spoon and is out if it falls.

clue.text: Turned back in the ship when one wants another route

definitions.text: Turned back in the ship when one wants another route

parts.words: Turned back in the ship when one wants another route
parts.note: a steering blade at the stern of a vessel is turned to change course

explanation.surface: Someone on board turns back when they want to go another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned back' suggests a reversal or a retreat; it is a part at the back of the vessel that is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged blade at a vessel's stern is swung to steer it onto a new course.

clue.text: Much gone into by students of otherworldly things

definitions.text: Much gone into by students of otherworldly things

parts.words: Much gone into by students of otherworldly things
parts.note: gone into suggests studied, but it means entered: mystics and mediums often enter dreamlike states

explanation.surface: A subject much researched by scholars of the supernatural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone into' looks like 'researched'; it means 'entered', as a medium enters a hypnotic state.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hypnotic, half-conscious states, often linked with mediums and mystics.

clue.text: Attacked badly-gave sad, muddled order

indicators.note: a muddled order is a jumbled arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer was furiously attacked after issuing a sad, confused command.
explanation.definitionFit: To maul or tear into something viciously, as a wild animal does, is to attack it badly.

clue.text: Presumably join one by going in through the tradesman's entrance?

definitions.text: Presumably join one by going in through the tradesman's entrance?

parts.words: Presumably join one by going in through the tradesman's entrance?
parts.note: the tradesman's entrance is the side door for workers; read jokingly, a worker gets in by enrolling with a trade organisation, and the thing joined is itself a joining

explanation.surface: Joining a household by sneaking in through the servants' door.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tradesman's entrance' is the British side door used by delivery people; here it hints at membership of a trade body.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction or merger is a joining, and a trade workers' association is also called by this word.

clue.text: It purrs and spins to steady -the rider

indicators.note: spins means the letters whirl round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat purrs and turns circles to calm the horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spins' looks like the cat's action, but it signals the anagram of IT PURRS.
explanation.definitionFit: This metal loop hung from a saddle holds the horseman's foot and keeps them steady.

clue.text: Rose in power when the Plantaganets fell!

definitions.text: Rose in power when the Plantaganets fell!

parts.words: Rose in power when the Plantaganets fell!
parts.note: rose reads as a verb, came to power, but is also the noun: the heraldic flower of the dynasty that followed the Plantagenets in 1485

explanation.surface: A dynasty came to the throne when the old royal house fell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a verb but is also the heraldic flower of Henry VII's royal house, which took the English throne in 1485.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VII founded this royal house after defeating Richard III, last of the Plantagenet line.

clue.text: Measures for those who drink like fish?

definitions.meaning: small units of liquid volume, a quarter of a pint

definitions.text: for those who drink like fish?
definitions.meaning: fish take in water through their breathing organs

explanation.surface: Drinks measures for heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink like fish' means drinking heavily; read literally, it is how fish take in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter-pint is a unit of liquid volume, and fish breathe through slits behind the head with the same name.

clue.text: How one went along with a swagger-stick, presumably?…

definitions.text: How one went along with a swagger-stick, presumably?…

parts.words: How one went along with a swagger-stick, presumably?…
parts.note: a swagger stick is an officer's cane; read jokingly, anyone carrying one walked with a swagger

explanation.surface: An officer with a cane walks along in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: A swagger-stick is a short cane carried by military officers; the joke takes 'swagger' literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with a swagger is to walk proudly with chest out, a pompous gait.

clue.text: Frequently belt the most rapacious part

indicators.note: part means only a stretch of the words most rapacious is taken

explanation.surface: Repeatedly beating someone is the greediest behaviour of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'moST RAPacious'.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone with a leather band is to hit them again and again with it.

clue.text: … Idly walking and talking -nonsense!

definitions.meaning: speaking at length in a confused, wandering way

explanation.surface: Walking idly while chattering away nonsensically.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiking aimlessly is one sense; speaking in a disjointed, wandering way is the other.

clue.text: Plays a big role in folklore

definitions.text: Plays a big role in folklore

parts.words: Plays a big role in folklore
parts.note: big role suggests an important part, but read literally the character is huge, an ogre of fairy tales

explanation.surface: Someone is important in traditional stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big role' sounds like a starring part; literally it is a huge character, as in Jack and the Beanstalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge humanlike figures are stock characters in folk tales and fairy stories.

clue.text: See 6down
A trebly old-fashioned term?

parts.note: an archaic word meaning three times over, so trebly in sense and dated in style

explanation.surface: A word that is very much out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trebly old-fashioned' reads as 'very dated'; it means a dated word for 'three times'.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adverb means on three occasions or to three times the extent.

clue.text: The bed of the sea?

parts.note: the bed of the sea suggests the ocean floor, but read literally it is where sailors sleep at sea

explanation.surface: The ocean floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed of the sea' looks like the seabed; it is the hanging canvas bed sailors slept in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors traditionally slept in hanging canvas or netting beds slung between hooks below decks.

clue.text: Plant borders? Barriers, rather

definitions.meaning: fences or obstacles that keep things apart

explanation.surface: Asking whether flower-bed edges are really more like fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant borders' reads as flower borders; here they are rows of shrubs grown as boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of shrubs planted as boundaries act as living fences and screens.

clue.text: Gets down to do some serious begging, perhaps!

definitions.text: Gets down to do some serious begging, perhaps!

parts.words: Gets down to do some serious begging, perhaps!
parts.note: gets down to suggests starting work in earnest, but here it means lowering oneself, as a pleader does on bended knee

explanation.surface: Someone settles down to beg in earnest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets down to' looks like 'starts'; it means physically dropping on bended knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone begging may drop onto bended knee before the person they implore.

clue.text: Garden implement lying round American dwelling

indicators.note: lying round means the tool's letters are laid around the next piece

parts.note: a hoe is a long-handled tool for weeding a garden
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A garden tool has been left out around an American home.
explanation.definitionFit: A home or residence is a place where one dwells.

clue.text: He stops drawing, too, in medical work

definitions.text: He stops drawing, too, in medical work

parts.words: He stops drawing, too, in medical work
parts.note: stops and drawing suggest an artist giving up, but read as fillings and extractions they are the work of a tooth doctor

explanation.surface: An artist gives up drawing to take up medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' means fills cavities and 'drawing' means pulling teeth, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth doctor fills cavities and extracts teeth as part of the job.

clue.text: Look twisted!

parts.note: look twisted reads as an order to appear warped, but it describes a facial expression contorted in pain or distaste

explanation.surface: An order to appear contorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' is a noun here: an expression on the face that is twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A contorted facial expression of pain or disgust is an ugly, twisted look.

clue.text: A kind of courage that's sensational, one might say!

definitions.text: A kind of courage that's sensational, one might say!

parts.words: A kind of courage that's sensational, one might say!
parts.note: sensational suggests thrilling, but literally it means carrying sensation: a word for boldness is also a fibre carrying feeling in the body

explanation.surface: Praising a particularly impressive act of bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensational' looks like 'thrilling' but literally means 'to do with sensation'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means boldness, and is also the fibre that carries sensation through the body.

clue.text: Changing sides, rage as one takes a different view

indicators.note: changing means the letters swap places into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone switching allegiance in a fury because they no longer agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing sides' reads as switching allegiance, but 'Changing' signals the anagram of SIDES + RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold an opposing opinion is to dissent from someone else's view.
